name: Willem Brask
aliases: the big man at the spear

physicalDetails.detail: Big, heavy through the shoulders, shorter than Sylvanas. Quilted jack too warm for the day, leather cap, fair stubble going grey. Hands cracked across the knuckles, right thumbnail split and black underneath. Face goes 'a bad colour under the stubble' when the cradle is mentioned; by morning grey with the night, soot on his face and jack. Carries a boar spear (broad leaf head, crossbar under it, ash shaft) held level across the lane like a farmer holds a gate against his own cattle.
Morning kit: a thick ledger under his arm, a little horn of ink on a cord round his neck, a pen behind his ear, ink stopper pulled with his teeth.

voiceMarkers.detail: Blunt village-captain speech: 'That's far enough. We've sick here. Nobody comes in armed, and nobody comes in I don't know.' First calls Sylvanas 'my lady', then repeats 'Ranger-General'. To Tobin's fever-diagnosis he clings ('It's fever. It's the time of year for it. Tobin says it's fever.'). Orders in two-word cracks once convinced ('Piers. Get your brother and the Aldon boys...', 'Dickon. ... Go on.'). Quiet when it lands: 'Cover his face, somebody.' Says things aloud as he writes, and when he reads back the name gets 'the middle wrong and then right'.

Father's voice to Tam ('Tam. What's this? What've you done?'); self-justifying calm in the dark ('In the morning. I'll have the whole of it in the morning.'); decisive once told: 'Tell me what to shut.' / 'Burn it, then. All of it. In Joss's yard, where they can see it. I'll answer for the flour.'

beliefs.belief: The sickness is fever, the time of year for it; Tobin says so.
beliefs.trueOrFalse: Wrong; he abandons it after Sylvanas's Millhaven account and the egg-stall cough.

beliefs.belief: Strangers who come armed are a threat to the village; nobody comes in who he does not know.
beliefs.trueOrFalse: Reversed by Sylvanas: he lets them in but lets the village see him with her.

beliefs.belief: Tam is a good lad he fed at his own table.
beliefs.trueOrFalse: Tam was a watcher; Brask took it hard: 'He sat next to my youngest and cut her meat for her.'

goalsAtChapterEnd.active: Finish going round the houses with the burned flour; recover the Hallams' and the alehouse's sacks; learn what Joss knows; tell the story right if anyone asks.
goalsAtChapterEnd.underlying: Keep his village from being Millhaven.

emotionalStateAtChapterEnd.state: Grey with the night, heavily steady; betrayed by a boy he fed at his table; committed. He has written the strangers' names so the tale can be told right.

decisionsThisChapter.detail: Barred the lane with his spear, then lowered it after Sylvanas named Millhaven and the cradle; named himself; had Dickon take the mage to Tobin.
Walked the village with Sylvanas and spoke to the pump women, publicly with her.
Came to the granary with torches after the commotion; named Tam; locked him in the stone cage by the pound at the bottom of Chapel Lane.

Before the 'morning' delay was challenged, he proposed to have Joss up first thing; after Jaina's and Sylvanas's warning, shut the granary and bakehouse overnight and ordered every sack of the man's flour in every house burned in Joss's yard; sent Piers and the Aldon boys house to house; sent Dickon with ponies after the cart sent to the ford for the Hallams and alehouse.
Stood at the yard gate with a slate or board recording each sack; at morning had the loft boards (with Jaina's ice) carried down and burned; wrote all four names in his ledger.

abilitiesDemonstrated.ability: Local authority: speaks to the pump women and the village follows; can raise Piers, the Aldon boys, Dickon and a bonfire in minutes; knows where the keys are (the cage key found by feel).

howOthersAddressHim.speaker: Tobin / villagers
howOthersAddressHim.pattern: 'Willem' (Tobin: 'Willem sent you?'; 'I said so to Willem.')

howOthersAddressHim.speaker: Sylvanas
howOthersAddressHim.pattern: 'Captain' (after he gives his name and rank); she says 'Captain' every time.

howHeAddressesOthers.pattern: 'Miss' as an afterthought; 'the mage' in the ledger ('The mage. Jaina. Proudmoore.')

bodyLanguagePatterns.detail: Thumb on the ash shaft; stops moving when he is struck by a fact ('The thumb stopped.'), slides up and down when he is uncertain; elbow thrust back to move the boy; holds the ledger shut against his chest with both hands as he held the spear; torch held low so the light comes from below and makes his face strange.

knowledge.detail: Knows his village, his militia, Tobin's fever theory; knows Joss's granary supplies the village; learns from Sylvanas that Millhaven emptied (sixty prints counted); learns from Jaina and Sylvanas that the flour is the carrier; says of Andorhal: 'That's the big granaries. Down the grain road, south and west, past the ford. Three days, with a cart. Everything in the south goes through Andorhal, one way or another. My barley goes through Andorhal.'
Does not know who sold Joss the flour; what Tam knew; or the full size of the contamination; he does not know the word 'necromancy' (never spoken to him).

arc.lie: It is fever, and strangers armed are the danger.
arc.truth: It is the flour; the armed strangers are the ones who can help.
arc.currentPosition: Chapter 4: lie gone; he acts on strangers' word and burns his own village's bread. Does not return on page (plan: only later appearance is a sworn letter for the defence in Chapter 23).
